title: Route Rollup & Token-slice Inspector: latency + token cost surface
creator: Juno Kim
description:
Purpose: design a compact 'Route Rollup & Token-slice Inspector' canvas that surfaces per-route and per-model variant latency, throughput and token-cost signals at multiple granularities (route-level rollups, per-request microtrace, and aggregated token-slices). This ticket captures the prototype, interaction flows, and chart specifications for handoff to frontend and runtime teams.

Background: customers want a single pane in Console where they can: (1) quickly assess if a given route is meeting latency SLOs and where tokens are being spent, (2) drill to example traces where KV-cache or batching caused variance, and (3) correlate recent rollouts with changes in P99/P95 and cost per 1k tokens. Existing dashboards are too wide and duplicate visualizations across model and route views — this inspector consolidates rollups, anomaly flags, and a lightweight microtrace timeline optimized for high-cardinality traffic.

Scope: design for desktop with responsive fallback. Deliverables: high-fidelity Figma canvas for inspector, a set of chart specs (list included below), interactive prototype showing drill flow from rollup -> trace -> rollout diff, accessibility color tokens, and a compact embeddable widget spec for per-model cards in the route list. Out of scope: server-side aggregation implementation and dedicated capacity autoscale controls (handled in ENG tickets).
comments: 2026-02-10 - Juno: Initial draft of canvas and interaction map uploaded to Figma (link in artifacts). Focused on three verticals: Rollup summary, Token-slice cost ribbon, Microtrace waterfall.

2026-02-11 - Lina: Design review with PM and runtime. Feedback: emphasize canary/rollout annotations and allow toggling model-variant overlays. Action: add clear legend for model variants and create a low-ink mode for heavy dashboards.

2026-02-12 - Juno: Incorporated review feedback. Split the token cost ribbon into 'chargeable tokens' vs 'internal KV/cache tokens'. Added 'anomaly marker' state with suggested thresholds. Ready for dev handoff review on 2026-02-14.

2026-02-12 - ENG-8812 (comment): Backend needs a new aggregated timeseries endpoint for token-slices (per 1s buckets) and an example sample payload attached (see artifacts). Requesting final field names for charting.
2026-02-12 - PM-5123: Suggested adding a low-power mode for customers with thousands of routes; propose sampling defaults and expand on user settings in future ticket.
chart_specs: Rollup Summary Card: single-line summary card showing 1m/5m/1h rollups for Requests/s, Avg latency, P95, P99, Cost per 1k tokens. Each metric shows delta vs previous window and a tiny sparkline (12 datapoints).

Token-slice Ribbon: stacked horizontal ribbon segmented by sequence-length buckets (0-32,33-128,129-512,513-2k,>2k). Y-axis is tokens/1000 and each segment color-encoded by cost rate. Hover shows absolute tokens, cost estimate, and top model variant contributors.

Latency Heatmap: 2D heatmap (x: timestamp 1h window, y: sequence-length buckets) showing median latency with percentile contours. Color scale uses perceptually uniform palette and has an accessible alternate (high-contrast) theme.

Microtrace Waterfall: compact per-request timeline that stacks token-generation phases: model-init, KV-lookup, batching-queue, kernel-runtime, network. Each phase has duration and token-range annotations; hover reveals full trace and associated request_id, model-variant, and rollout tag.

Model-variant Overlay: per-rollup timeseries overlay that can toggle up to 3 variants. Overlays use dashed lines and semi-transparent fills; legend indicates rollout percentage and time ranges for canary windows.
Anomaly Timeline: event strip below charts that surfaces deployment events, capacity outages, and automatic fallbacks. Clicking an event pre-filters the rollup window to +/ - 15m.
Cost Breakdown Donut (compact): shows percentage contribution across model variants and token buckets; clicking a slice filters the main rollup to that subset.

Throughput vs Latency Scatter: aggregated points for recent requests binned by per-minute throughput; point size = avg token length, color = model variant. Includes linear regression line and toggle for percentile shading.
interaction_notes: Entry point: route list -> 'Inspect' button opens inspector as right-side modal. Secondary entry: from model page 'Open route rollup' to compare all routes hitting a model.
Drill flow: Rollup Summary -> click sparkline to open heatmap -> click heatmap cell to load example microtraces -> click trace to open full trace in Trace Viewer.
Filtering: persistent filters for time range, model-variant, and sequence-length. Filters are baked into shareable URL.
Performance considerations: default to sampled microtraces (1% of requests) with 'Show all' toggle for admin users. Use pre-aggregated token-slices to power ribbon and heatmap charts.

Rollout integration: visually annotate rollout windows; when a rollout is active show variant contribution in Rollup Summary and provide 'compare pre/post' quick toggle that diffs P95/P99 and cost per 1k tokens.
Accessibility: all charts expose numeric tooltips and keyboard focusable drill targets. Color scale paired with pattern overlays for colorblind users.
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype exists and demonstrates the full drill flow (rollup -> heatmap -> microtrace) and variant overlay behavior
Design tokens and accessible color palettes documented in Figma and Confluence
Chart specs above reviewed and signed off by ENG leads (ENG-8812) and PM (PM-5123)
Frontend dev has a completed handoff folder with component variants, copy, and micro-interaction notes
Usability test: 5 engineers/PMs run a 15-minute task (identify a rollout-caused P99 regression) with >=80% success rate
